title: AI Architecture Decision Records: Governing Model, Vendor, and Boundary Choices (2026)

questions.question: A model deprecates, outputs shift silently, and prices jump — and the ADR that chose it helps nobody. What was missing from it?
options: A longer model name
More benchmark screenshots
Trust that choices stay valid
Revert triggers: cost, latency, classification, review date
questions.explanation: Static ADRs expire with conditions. This lesson records the boundary conditions that keep decisions governable.

questions.question: Why does AI-ADR-003 fail validation?
options: Its efficient model tier is forbidden for embeddings
The owner is empty and all four trigger categories are missing
Its review date is in the future, so proposed ADRs cannot be checked
Its public data classification requires a dedicated endpoint
questions.explanation: The ADR has an empty owner and an empty trigger_conditions dictionary. validate_adr reports the missing owner plus cost, capability, compliance, and deprecation trigger gaps.

questions.question: What monthly cost does project_monthly_cost calculate for AI-ADR-001?
options: $2,000.00, because the ceiling is the projected spend
$115.20, because only prompt tokens are billed
$230.40, combining prompt and completion costs at 8,000 requests per day
$1,152.00, because the 30-day multiplier applies twice

questions.question: What warning does validate_adr produce for AI-ADR-002?
options: The ADR is rejected because frontier models have no trigger conditions
The owner is missing, so no cost is computed
The review date is invalid because it uses an ISO date
Projected monthly cost is $20,520, above the $5,000 ceiling
questions.explanation: The 18,000-token prompt and 4,000-token completion at 120 requests per day cost $9,720 and $10,800 respectively. The $20,520 projection exceeds the ceiling, so validation passes but emits a cost warning.

questions.question: Which ADRs contribute to print_register_summary's accepted monthly-spend total?
options: AI-ADR-001 and AI-ADR-002, because both have status accepted
All three ADRs, because proposed decisions are included for planning
Only AI-ADR-003, because it is the one still under review
None, because the register counts only deprecated decisions
questions.explanation: The summary adds projected costs only when status equals accepted. ADR-001 and ADR-002 are accepted; the proposed embedding ADR is displayed but excluded from the accepted-spend total.

questions.question: What does the portfolio summary do with AI-ADR-003's proposed status?
options: It marks the ADR overdue and adds its cost to accepted spend
It displays the proposed entry but excludes it from accepted spend and overdue-accepted review alerts
It automatically changes proposed to accepted after validation
It retires the ADR because its trigger conditions are empty
questions.explanation: build_register validates every entry, but print_register_summary adds cost and overdue markers only for status='accepted'. Proposed ADR-003 remains visible without being treated as an approved decision.
